title: A quadratic harmonic envelope leaves under 2.2 percent of test signal power in Kepler KIC 3230227 fits
abstract: We test a known weak frequency in Kepler KIC 3230227. We allow a smooth change in the sine and cosine coefficients at the 13th orbital harmonic. We also fit other orbital harmonics, quarter trends, and four known frequencies. A quadratic envelope leaves 2.175 to 2.194 percent of the sampled test signal power with 80 harmonics. A fourth-degree envelope leaves about 0.010 percent. Fits with 40 harmonics give similar loss. Joint flux fits have large conditional errors as the envelope degree increases. This is a limit on signal separation under the stated models. It does not establish an instrumental cause, reject a known mode, or find a new object. No independent instrument is used.

display.caption: Left: minimum test signal power retained over all phases. Right: joint signal amplitudes and one conditional quarter-cluster standard error. Errors do not include model uncertainty.
